The task we learn on
An e-mail from the commercial director: “How did sales go this year? Why did advertising pay off worse in the second half? And why so many returns in the autumn? I need one page by Friday.”
We spend the lesson answering this e-mail. At the end we have the report page.

Part 1 • what data is

Where data lives at work

Spreadsheets
Excel, Google Sheets: sales, budget, plan
AI writes formulas and pivots
Exports
CSV from a CRM, accounting, ad accounts, YouTube Studio
file into a chat, AI writes code
Databases
CRM, website, warehouse: millions of rows, updated daily
AI writes an SQL query
Text
reviews, e-mails, support chats, surveys
AI reads and sorts into themes
Documents
PDF invoices, contracts, partner reports
AI pulls the numbers into a table
Events and logs
clicks, orders by the minute, calls
usually an analyst queries the database
Most often you have a spreadsheet or an export. Sometimes text. Less often a database. Today we cover all three.

Part 1 • what a table is made of

One row: what the record is and what it measures

order_datechannelcategoryregionwarehouseordersrevenuead_spendreturns
2025-01-05EmailElectronicsNorthN211980.001
datecategorycategorycategorycategorynumber, pcsnumber, $number, $number, pcs
A row is the sales of one channel for one category, region and warehouse on one day. Not an order, not a customer.
Categories are what we slice by: channel, region, warehouse. Breakdowns are built on them.
Numbers are what we add and divide. Each has its unit: dollars or pieces.
First question for any file: what is one row? Get it wrong and every “average per customer” is wrong.

Part 1 • real data

Four traps in real data, three of them in our file

A duplicated row
2025-03-19 · Social · Home · 3,890.5 ×2
revenue is inflated by this amount
A date as text
10/05/2025 ← 2025-05-10?
10 May or 5 October? Depends on the format
Zero or missing?
Email · ad_spend = 0
Email has no ads. The model called these zeros “missing”
Mixed units
1,200 (RUB) and 15 ($) in one column
a real-life example: they can’t be added
The model often finds these, but doesn’t always understand them. The data owner knows what a zero means and which date is right.

Demo 1 live • 5 minutes

We do it live: from the file to a formula in a cell

  1. Upload northstar_2025.xlsx to ChatGPT
  2. Prompt 1 — describe the file (slide 11)
  3. Prompt 2 — the “Ad return” sheet (slide 13)

Weak / good • seasonality

“One number for the slide” — and the model picked the loudest

✗ Weak “How much did sales grow this year? One number for the slide.”
+161.7% is December vs January. January is the weakest month, December is sales season. It sounds like growth; it’s the season.
Revenue by month
✓ Good “Compute growth three ways, give the base and period for each. Which number goes on the slide and why?”
Three numbers with their base and a verdict: “the second half is about 40% above the first”.

Five questions, five charts — all from our file

line

sorted bars

histogram

Part 3 • what we found

Two problems the annual total doesn’t show

1. Social: spend went up, revenue didn’t
Social ad spend by month, $
Social revenue by month, $
Second half vs first: spend +184%, revenue +43%. Revenue per $1 of ads: 4 → 2.
2. Warehouse N2: returns and damage complaints
Return rate by month, %
From September N2 returns are about 26%, others about 5%. Almost half of N2 reviews are about damaged parcels.
The number shows where; the text explains why. Reviews are data too.

Part 3 • a slide-ready chart

You edit a chart with words, like text

Before: the default chart
PromptRework this chart for a slide: the title states the finding, bars sorted, value labels on the bars, no legend and no gridlines, one accent colour for N2, everything else grey. Explain in 3 points what you changed.
After: 36 seconds later
Title = finding. “Almost 9× more” instead of “Review themes”.
One colour. N2 blue, the rest grey — the eye finds the point at once.
Values on the bars, no legend or grid.

Part 3 • quick / under control #3

The first line is a scenario, not a forecast. Read the assumptions

Quick The first line of the answer to “If we cut the Social budget in half from January, how much do we save and how much revenue do we lose per quarter?”
“Revenue loss — 122.5k” in the first line. That assumes revenue falls together with the budget.
✓ Under control The same answer, paragraphs below
The model itself says: the file can’t show the real loss; you need a test with a control group.

Part 4 • SQL line by line

SQL reads almost like a plain sentence

PromptThe database has a videos table: length and views of every video. Write an SQL query: which video length gets the most views? Explain every line.
1
SELECT duration_bucket,
what to show: length
2
COUNT(*) AS videos,
how many videos in the group
3
MEDIAN(views) AS typical
typical views: half above, half below
4
FROM videos
from which table
5
GROUP BY duration_bucket;
what to group by
Describe the tables in the prompt. Without it the model guesses column names and the query fails.
GenAI Basics • Lesson 08 • AI for Data Analysis25 / 31
Part 4 • the result and the trap

Long videos 12× more popular? No: big channels make them

First query: typical views by length
20–40 minutes gets 12× more than short videos? Compared with ordinary videos of the same channel, they are only 3% above usual. Big channels simply make long videos more often.
Second query: a video vs its own channel’s usual video
1.0 means the same as the channel’s usual video. Every length is about 1.0.
GenAI Basics • Lesson 08 • AI for Data Analysis26 / 31
Part 4 • where data comes from

Look for an Export button first, then an API. Scraping is the last option

1. Export
An “Export to Excel / CSV” button exists almost everywhere: CRM, accounting, ad accounts, YouTube Studio, Google Analytics.
fast · legal · no code
2. Official API
{ "title": "Kitchen Basics", "subscriberCount": "184000", "videoCount": "412" }
A program asks the service and gets an answer like this. AI writes a script that turns it into table rows.
this is how the slide 24 channel database was collected
3. Scraping
A program reads website pages like a person would. Before you do it, check:
  • the site’s terms allow it
  • no personal data
  • you don’t overload the site
Ask the AI: “What official export or API does system X have to download a year of sales?”

Part 5 • data and privacy

What you may upload to a chat

OK: practice, public, anonymised data
like Northstar; any service
Careful: internal company data
only in the work account (ChatGPT Business/Enterprise, Claude Team/Enterprise, Google Workspace) — data is not used for training there
Not without approval: customers, staff, finance, health
personal data — only in an approved environment with the data owner’s consent
Before uploading, delete unneeded columns: names, phones, e-mails. Sales analysis doesn’t need them.
In personal accounts, training on your data depends on settings: ChatGPT — “Improve the model for everyone”, Gemini — “Keep Activity”, Claude — only if you allowed it.
